newsitem.title: USA: IMF welcomes Ukraine's launch of new currency.
newsitem.headline: IMF welcomes Ukraine's launch of new currency.

text.p: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus on Friday welcomed Ukraine's introduction of a new currency and said the country was on its way to an economic recovery.

"The sound financial policies pursued by Ukraine so far in 1996 have helped reduce inflation and stabilize the exchange rate," Camdessus said in a statement. Ukraine introduced its new hryvnya currency earlier this month and asked the the IMF for a $1.5 billion stabilization fund to back it up.
"The management of the IMF welcomes the introduction of the hryvnya," he said. But his statement made no comment on Ukraine's request for a currency stabilization fund.
He said Ukraine's sound financial policies and structural economic reforms, particularly its privatisation, have "helped pave the way toward the recovery of the economy."

An IMF mission is due to visit Ukraine next week. IMF resident representative Alex Sundakov told Reuters this week the Fund team would concentrate on Ukraine's request for a $2.5-to-$3 billion, extended fund facility, three-year loan.

He would not comment on Kiev's request for a currency stabilization fund. Ukraine has already borrowed about $485 billion from the IMF under a one-year, $864 million stand-by loan approved by the Fund in May.
